text:
morgan: Heads up — noticed big sparkline/frame drops on canary 2 in eu-console around 09:04 UTC. Charts freeze for ~700-1200ms on initial paint. Metric panels only, list pages ok.

jamie: saw that too, reproduced on my laptop. looks like main-thread work spikes during render handoff. devtools shows heavy parse time and long task.

liam: grabbing profiles now. flame shows big chunk in `telemetry-client/init` and `compressTelemetry()` on startup.

tess: that's odd — telemetry client didn't change in this rollout AFAIK. which bundle did canary pull?

morgan: canary pulled `console-web@2026.03.11-canary-42` (route: prefetched + prefetch-priority=low). We switched telemetry sampler to v2 in that build.

liam: here's the top of the CPU stack (abbrev):
```
telemetryClient.init -> index.js:142
compressTelemetry -> worker.js:88
chartRenderer.update -> sparkline.js:67
renderHandoff -> hydration.js:21
```

kyle: pinging @maria and @frontend-ux but initial suspicion: telemetry v2 includes a sync compression path that runs on main thread when worker fallback hits.

jamie: yep worker fallback happened for me in incognito (no SharedWorker). that explains main thread work.

tess: can we short-circuit compression when charts are visible? or offload to setTimeout/yield until after first paint?

liam: quick fix idea — guard telemetry init with `if (!document.hidden) scheduleIdle(() => initTelemetry())` and ensure `scheduleIdle` uses requestIdleCallback + fallback microtask. reduces startup pressure.

morgan: agree. also we should change prefetch priority for this canary — prefetched telemetry lib is huge now (120kb gz) and inflates chunk parse.

kyle: creating rollback canary with telemetry init deferred and prefetch disabled. Deploy bot: @deploy-bot can we roll back canary tag `2026.03.11-canary-42` and promote `canary-41` to testers only?

deploy-bot: deploy request received: rollback canary `2026.03.11-canary-42` -> approving. ETA ~6m.

maria: long term: we need a policy for third-party libs that can run on main thread. routing/quotas should prefer low-latency routes for charts with minimal prefetched deps. maybe add `routeHints` in manifest.

jamie: +1. also telemetry team — can we provide a worker-first build or split the compress module into async chunk that loads after initial render?

tess: I'll open a small PR to defer telemetry init (patch + test) and add a canary rollback playbook entry.

morgan: thanks. keeping this thread for postmortem notes — add perf traces here once rollback done.

kyle: noted. ops-bot: posting rollback timeline to #incidents for visibility.

ops-bot: rollback started at 09:11 UTC, canary traffic shifted. will post final when verified.

morgan: verified on canary-41 re: no sparkline stalls. rough perf numbers: first-paint frames dropped reduced from 12% -> 1.8% on test traces.

liam: filing follow-up tasks: 1) telemetry: worker-first build or split compress -> EXP-4012, 2) platform: routeHints + prefetch policy -> PLT-3321, 3) devex: add canary rollback playbook snippet -> DX-121.

tess: PR #6789 opened to defer init, added unit + integration smoke test. merging after green.

maria: we'll discuss `routeHints` on Monday infra sync — goal: ensure metric-heavy routes avoid pulling large agent bundles at load.

morgan: thanks all. participants: @morgan @jamie @liam @tess @kyle @maria @deploy-bot @ops-bot :thumbsup
